## Question 1

:::{.callout-warning}
## Binomial Probabilities

A quiz has 12 multiple-choice questions, each with 4 options. A student guesses on every question, so $p=0.25$.

Compute in R with `dbinom()`:

1. $P(X=3)$
2. $P(X\le 3)$, using `sum(dbinom(0:3, 12, 0.25))`
3. $P(X\ge 6)$
:::

---

## Question 2

:::{.callout-warning}
## Mean and Standard Deviation of a Binomial Variable

For the same quiz:

1. Compute $\mu=np$ and $\sigma=\sqrt{npq}$ in R.
2. Would scoring 7 or more correct answers by guessing be unusual? Use the $\mu\pm 2\sigma$ rule to justify your answer.
:::

---

## Question 3

:::{.callout-warning}
## Poisson Distribution

A help desk receives an average of 4 calls per hour.

Compute in R:

1. $P(X=6)$ in a given hour with `dpois()`
2. $P(X\le 2)$ with `ppois()`
3. $P(X\ge 5)$

State in one sentence which assumption of the Poisson distribution may be violated at lunchtime.
:::
